steps.decision: Rebuild both totals before touching the wrong value. A mean and a standard deviation cannot be edited; totals can.
Both numbers move. The reports describe candidates using only 655 or only 745; one of them takes the wrong mass out and the other puts the right one in.
Divide by 18, the number of fish, which has not changed: a correction replaces a value, it does not remove one.

options: 18, because correcting a mass does not change how many fish were weighed
17, because one fish has been taken out of the set
19, because a new mass has been added
whyMenu.explain: Only a removal or an addition changes $n$. A correction swaps one value for another, so the count is untouched.

steps.decision: Squares come out of a sum of squares and squares go in. Adding the raw difference of 90 is the attempt the examiners saw most often, and it is what makes this the hardest part of the paper.

steps.decision: Both totals first, as always. The standard deviation is only there so that the sum of squares can be recovered.
The score itself leaves the first total and its square leaves the second. Subtracting 47 from both is the slip that spoils the standard deviation.
A removal changes the count. This is the difference between a removal and a correction, and it is the line that is most often missing.
The mean rises, because the score that left was below the old mean of 58. Always check the direction against common sense.
The spread falls sharply, from 4 to 2.34, because the score that left was the one furthest from the mean.

findTheMistake.stem: Rónán was asked for the corrected mean mass of the 18 trout (mean 940 g, one mass recorded as 655 instead of 745). His working:
studentWorking: corrected sum of x = 15980 - 655 + 745 = 16070
corrected mean = 16070 over 18 = 892.78
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 1 multiplies by 17 instead of 18. All 18 fish were weighed; correcting one mass does not take a fish out of the set.
findTheMistake.feedback: The correction itself is handled properly: one mass out, the other in, which is the step the examiners say candidates most often get wrong. The method mark for the recovery is lost at line 1. Multiply by the number of fish the question names, and the corrected mean is 945 grams.

findTheMistake.stem: Aoibhín was asked for the corrected standard deviation of the 25 reading times (mean 62, standard deviation 12, the entry 39 should have been 54). Her working:
studentWorking: sum of x squared = 25(12 squared + 62 squared) = 99700
corrected sum of x squared = 99700 + (54 - 39) = 99715
corrected mean = 1565 over 25 = 62.6
sd = square root of (99715 over 25 minus 62.6 squared) = 8.36
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 2 adds the raw difference of 15. A sum of squares changes by the difference of the squares: $54^{2} - 39^{2} = 2916 - 1521$.
correction: sd = square root of (101095 over 25 minus 62.6 squared) = 11.18
findTheMistake.feedback: The recovery of $\sum x^{2}$ and the corrected mean are both right, so two marks are safe. The method-and-working mark is lost at line 2: what leaves a sum of squares is a square, and what enters it is a square. Examiners report this as the commonest attempt on this part. With 101095 in place the answer is 11.18 minutes.

findTheMistake.stem: Seán was asked for the standard deviation of the 11 scores left after the shooter who scored 47 was disqualified. His working:
studentWorking: sum of x = 696, sum of x squared = 40560
after the disqualification: sum of x = 649, sum of x squared = 38351
mean = 649 over 12 = 54.08
sd = square root of (38351 over 12 minus that mean squared) = 16.46
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 3 still divides by 12. One shooter has gone, so the count is 11, and that count is used again in line 4.
correction: after the disqualification: n = 11, sum of x = 649, sum of x squared = 38351
sd = square root of (38351 over 11 minus 59 squared) = 2.34
findTheMistake.feedback: Both totals are adjusted correctly, including the square, so the first two marks are safe. The count was not adjusted with them. Write $n$ beside every total you produce, and the remaining shooters' mean is 59 with a standard deviation of 2.34.

findTheMistake.stem: Pádraig was asked for the corrected mean of 30 test scores (mean 52; a score of 41 should have been 47). His working:
studentWorking: sum of x = 52 x 29 = 1508
corrected sum of x = 1508 - 41 + 47 = 1514
corrected mean = 1514 over 30 = 50.47
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 1 rebuilds the total from 29 scores. A correction swaps one score for another, so all 30 are still in the set.
findTheMistake.feedback: The swap itself is right, one score out and the other in, so its mark is safe. The rebuilt total is lost at line 1: multiply by the count the question names, and the corrected mean is 52.2.

findTheMistake.stem: Gráinne was asked for the corrected standard deviation of 12 values (mean 40, standard deviation 8; the value 42 should have been 30). Her working:
studentWorking: sum of x squared = 12(8 squared + 40 squared) = 19968
corrected sum of x squared = 19968 + (42 - 30) squared = 20112
corrected mean = 468 over 12 = 39
sd = square root of (20112 over 12 minus 39 squared) = 12.45
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 2 adds the square of the difference. A sum of squares changes by the difference of the squares: $42^{2}$ comes out and $30^{2}$ goes in.
correction: sd = square root of (19104 over 12 minus 39 squared) = 8.43
findTheMistake.feedback: The recovery of the sum of squares is right, so its two marks are safe. Line 2 squares the difference, the slip the Summer 2025 report describes, and the corrected total and the answer are lost. Take $42^{2}$ out and put $30^{2}$ in, and the answer is 8.43.

findTheMistake.stem: Eoin was asked for the standard deviation of the 10 values left after the value 30 is removed from a set of 11 (mean 19, standard deviation 7). His working:
studentWorking: sum of x = 209, sum of x squared = 11(7 squared + 19 squared) = 4510
after the removal: sum of x = 179, sum of x squared = 4510 - 900 = 3610
mean = 179 over 11 = 16.27
sd = square root of (3610 over 11 minus 16.27 squared) = 7.96
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Line 3 still divides by 11. One value has gone, so the count is 10, and line 4 needs it too.
correction: sum of x = 209, sum of x squared = 4510
after the removal: n = 10, sum of x = 179, sum of x squared = 3610
sd = square root of (3610 over 10 minus 17.9 squared) = 6.37
findTheMistake.feedback: Both totals are adjusted correctly, the square included, so the first marks are safe. The count was not adjusted with them. Write $n$ beside every total you produce, and the mean of the 10 is 17.9 with a standard deviation of 6.37.

prompts.prompt: The three-line table to draw before adjusting any data set.
prompts.answer: A row for $n$, a row for $\sum x$ and a row for $\sum x^{2}$, filled in before the change and again after it.

prompts.prompt: A value $a$ is corrected to $b$. How do the two totals change?
prompts.answer: $\sum x$ changes by $b - a$; $\sum x^{2}$ changes by $b^{2} - a^{2}$. The count does not change.

prompts.prompt: Which of a correction, a removal and an addition changes $n$?
prompts.answer: A removal lowers $n$ by one and an addition raises it by one. A correction leaves $n$ alone, because one value is swapped for another.

prompts.prompt: You have corrected $\sum x^{2}$. Which mean goes into the formula next?
prompts.answer: The corrected mean. The old mean belongs to the uncorrected data and using it mixes two different sets.

prompts.prompt: A value below the mean is removed from a set. Which way does the mean move?
prompts.answer: Up. Taking out something below the centre pulls the centre upwards.

prompts.prompt: A value far from the mean is replaced by one at the mean. Which way does the standard deviation move?
prompts.answer: Down. One of the distances from the mean has been cut to nothing, so the spread shrinks.

prompts.prompt: What is wrong with adjusting $\sum x^{2}$ by the raw difference between the two values?
prompts.answer: A sum of squares only ever gains or loses squares. The change is $b^{2} - a^{2}$, not $b - a$.

prompts.prompt: How do you get $\sum x^{2}$ back from $n$, the mean and the standard deviation?
The order of the last three steps once the totals are adjusted.
prompts.answer: Fix $n$, divide for the new mean, then substitute both into $\sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sum x^{2}}{n} - \bar{x}^{2}}$ and take the root.

prompts.prompt: A value equal to the mean is added to a set. What happens to the mean and to the standard deviation?
prompts.answer: The mean is unchanged. The standard deviation falls slightly, because the same total spread is now shared over one more value.

prompts.prompt: A value $a$ is corrected to $b$. By how much does $\sum x^{2}$ change?
How do you rebuild $\sum x^{2}$ from $n$, the mean and the standard deviation?
